title: policy-eval-entropy-caused-intermittent-hosted-to-private-surge
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple customers reported intermittent spikes where requests that should have been routed to Hosted model variants were routed to customers' Private pools during a regional autoscaling event. The misroutes increased latency and caused model incompatibility errors. Investigation shows the policy evaluation path can produce nondeterministic tie-breaks under concurrent policy syncs which causes transient wrong-tier selection.
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Deploy tenant with both hosted and private model variants and tenant-affinity overrides in us-west-2.
2. Simulate a capacity pressure event on Hosted (scale down then burst traffic) while concurrently updating a tenant policy (rollout change) with short TTL on policy cache.
3. Send high QPS traffic with variable session ids to exercise affinity hashing.
4. Observe a subset of requests routed to Private variants despite hosted capacity being available and eligible in the routing decision logs. Correlate with policy-sync timestamps in tracing.
5. Reproduce more reliably by forcing simultaneous policy syncs across routing nodes (example harness attached in links).
root_cause: Race in the policy merge/evaluation path: when policy deltas arrive concurrently, the policy engine performs a merge that leaves transient 'priority entropy' in the effective priority list. The tie-breaker uses a runtime entropy seed (timestamp-based) to pick between equal-priority candidates; under concurrent syncs this yields nondeterministic selection that can favor Private pools due to ordering. Additionally, a short policy cache TTL and asynchronous policy propagate path mean different routing nodes make different decisions for the same request window, producing customer-visible misroutes.
mitigation: 1. Emergency: increase policy cache TTL from 5s to 60s for affected regions to reduce sync churn.
2. Feature-flag: disable timestamp entropy tie-breaker and fall back to deterministic tenant-hash tie-breaker for the next release.
3. Rollback policy rollout for impacted tenants where possible and communicate mitigation to affected customers.
4. Add temporary routing shim to reject cross-tier routing when the route is ambiguous (fail closed to hosted) until the fix is deployed.
proposed_fix: Replace the timestamp-seeded entropy tie-breaker with a stable tie-breaker based on tenant_id + request_affinity_hash and make policy merge atomic by applying an explicit merge-order invariant. Add a policy-sync vector clock to ensure nodes apply deltas in the same effective order. Implement end-to-end deterministic routing tests and a canary that asserts no cross-tier misroutes under synthetic concurrency. Include a migration toggle to roll back quickly if unexpected regressions appear.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for deterministic tie-breaker behavior across edge cases (equal priority candidates, missing affinity fields).
- Integration test that simulates concurrent policy deltas across 10 routing nodes and validates per-request deterministic selection.
- Load test with autoscaling events in staging to reproduce previous misroute signature and confirm it's resolved.
- Regression tests in CI that run the policy-sync fuzz harness nightly.
- Post-deploy synthetic canary traffic comparing routing decisions between canary and control clusters for 24 hours.
rollout_plan: 1. Merge patch behind feature flag and run full CI (unit + integration).
2. Deploy to staging; execute load and chaos tests for 48h.
3. Canary deploy in us-west-2 to 5% of traffic with monitoring alerts on cross-tier routing ratio, latency spike, and model-compat errors.
4. If canary passes for 24h with no regression, ramp to 50% and then 100% regionally, then proceed to global rollout.
5. Coordinate with CSMs for affected customers; keep rollback playbook ready (feature-flag off + TTL revert).
